entries.core_move: Represent a continuous-time signal as shifted impulse components whose locations and weights encode its time-domain values for later LTI impulse-response analysis.
Express a continuous-time signal as a continuum of shifted impulses using the sifting identity $x(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}x(\tau)\delta(t-\tau)\,d\tau$.
Assign the weight $x(\tau)$ to each shifted impulse $\delta(t-\tau)$ in the continuous-time decomposition so the impulse continuum can be passed through an LTI system by superposition.

entries.lesson_title: From Impulse Decomposition to System Output
entries.core_move: Convert a weighted shifted-impulse input decomposition into the corresponding LTI output by replacing each shifted impulse with the matching shifted, scaled impulse response and superposing the responses.

Derive the continuous-time convolution integral $y(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}x(\tau)h(t-\tau)\,d\tau$ by applying linearity and time invariance to the weighted shifted-impulse decomposition of an input signal.
